terra.problem: The passage says the two disciples heard John, but does not say he addressed the words to them.
The claim that the title Son of David appears elsewhere in the Gospels needs a reference.
John's quoted statement has five words, not four.
Andrew first found Simon, but the text does not say Simon was the first person he went looking for.
The texting joke presents a modern option as something Andrew could have done, rather than as a comparison with modern life.
The passage does not record Simon speaking, but that does not establish that he had not said a word.
The passage says Moses wrote about the One in the Law, not that he wrote the whole Law. Calling Moses Israel's leader also needs a reference outside this passage.
The text does not say Philip delivered his words in one breath.
Calling Moses Israel's leader is a fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
Philip's reply, “Come and see,” has three words, not two.
The passage does not establish that Nathanael had never spoken to Jesus before this.
Nathanael has already spoken to Philip, so it is not before he has said anything at all.
The explanation assumes the baker's guess came from a different story, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
“A moment earlier” adds a specific time interval the passage does not give.
Acts 2:3 describes tongues like flames of fire; the explanation drops the comparison and calls them tongues of fire.
